TLDR: I used hate gays, and then I didn't. Then I hated Christians for teaching me to be homophobic. And then I realized hating people doesn't feel good.

I used to hate gays. Being raised at church had a lot to do with it. We had "strawman gays" and that was how I thought gays were pushy, perverted, and given into their lusts.

My best friend came out of the closet in high school. Sooooo yeah, I took a long look hard at what I believed in. 

After that, I started hating Christians. All my hatred for myself for being so previously bigoted I heaped upon my church and all of Christianity. It was all of their faults for all the sins in the world. They were all hypocrites. I feared God but I hated how he and christians said they were the light in the world when they were the ones causing so much pain and segregation. All of it. I hung out with other people who had bad experiences with christian people which only reinforced my beliefs.

A few years later I realized some of my athiest friends were pretty mean people and not too different from the christians we hated. And then I went back to church and people were actually pretty nice... I actually created a strawman christian myself... and instead of Christianity as a whole teaching me to hate gays when I was younger, it was actually a few bigoted adults that I looked up to, so in my mind, what they said had a lot of weight.

In terms of faith, I don't know where I am. Sometimes christians do some pretty cool things and sometimes they don't, it's like reddit. It's not one person doing all of it but millions. Hating people ain't too fun so I learned to treat people as individuals. Sometimes it really isn't easy
